biography: Jimmy Thomson, a name now whispered with respect in Ginetta circles, didn't emerge from the silver spoon of motorsport royalty. His father, a mechanic in a small Yorkshire garage, instilled in him a love for engines and speed from a young age. While other kids played football, Jimmy was tearing around the local scrapyard in a makeshift go-kart built from salvaged parts. He entered his first karting race at 14, funded by his paper route earnings, and although he finished last, the fire was lit. A pivotal moment came at 18 when, during a local hill climb, his raw talent caught the eye of a Ginetta team manager. He was offered a spot in their junior program, a lifeline he seized with both hands. Now, at 26, Thomson is a seasoned Ginetta driver, consistently challenging for podiums and on the cusp of a major breakthrough.
drivingStyle: Thomson's driving style is best described as 'calculated aggression'. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers. Instead, he meticulously studies track data, searching for the slightest advantage. He excels at managing tire wear and maintaining consistent lap times, gradually building pressure on his rivals until they crack. His approach to corners is smooth and precise, prioritizing exit speed over late braking heroics. He's a master of defensive driving, making it incredibly difficult for anyone to pass him.

rivalries.reason: A heated on-track incident at Brands Hatch in 2022, where Alvarez aggressively forced Thomson off the track, led to a lingering animosity. Thomson feels Alvarez's driving is reckless and dangerous.

Dubois consistently outperforms Thomson in qualifying, forcing him to fight his way through the pack. This has created a competitive tension, as Thomson believes he has the edge in race pace if he could only start higher up.
Beaumont is a Ginetta veteran and sees Thomson as a 'young upstart'. He often uses aggressive tactics to intimidate Thomson on the track, leading to several close calls and a simmering rivalry.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, knitted by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to classical music (specifically Mozart) for 30 minutes before each session to calm his nerves.
Has a specific routine for cleaning his visor, believing it affects his visibility and concentration.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about luck, it's about maximizing every opportunity. You make your own luck."
careerHighlight: Winning the Ginetta GT4 SuperCup race at Silverstone in 2021. He started 8th after a poor qualifying, but masterfully navigated the chaos to take the lead on the final lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2020 season at Donington Park. The incident cost him a chance to win the championship.
